controls.description: Publicly reachable without login, purchase, or a support request.
controls.title: Training-data documentation is posted on the developer's website

controls.description: Coverage is per system, not per company. A developer shipping three models needs documentation covering all three.
controls.title: Documentation exists for every publicly available system or service

requirements.description: The developer must publish documentation of the data used to train the system on its own internet website, on or before the system is made publicly available to Californians. A description supplied privately, on request, or only to enterprise customers does not discharge the duty — the obligation is to publish.
requirements.title: Post training-data documentation on the developer's own website

controls.title: Sources or owners of each dataset are named
Whether datasets were purchased or licensed is stated
Collection time period stated, with notice if collection is ongoing
Dates each dataset was first used in development are stated

requirements.description: The documentation must identify the sources or owners of the datasets, whether the developer purchased or licensed them, the time period during which the data was collected — with notice if collection is ongoing — and the dates the datasets were first used in development.
requirements.title: Identify where the training data came from

controls.title: Number of data points stated, at least as a general range
Copyright, trademark, patent, or public-domain status described

controls.description: This is the disclosure most likely to be wrong by omission: scraped web corpora routinely contain personal information whether or not it was sought.
controls.title: Presence of personal information (sec. 1798.140) disclosed
Presence of aggregate consumer information (sec. 1798.140) disclosed

requirements.description: The documentation must state the number of data points — general ranges are acceptable — whether the datasets include material protected by copyright, trademark, or patent or are entirely in the public domain, and whether they include personal information or aggregate consumer information as those terms are defined in Civil Code sec. 1798.140.
requirements.title: Describe what the training data contains

controls.title: How the datasets further the system's intended purpose is described
Cleaning, processing, or modification described, with its purpose
Use of synthetic data generation disclosed

requirements.description: The documentation must describe how the datasets further the intended purpose of the system, any cleaning, processing, or other modification the developer performed — including its purpose and whether it altered the structure or qualities of the data — and whether the system used or continuously uses synthetic data generation.
requirements.title: Describe how the data was used and modified

controls.description: A named owner and a monitored trigger, not an intention to remember.
controls.title: Retraining or fine-tuning triggers a documentation review
Published documentation identifies the system version it covers

requirements.description: A new version, release, or update that materially changes functionality or performance — including the result of retraining or fine-tuning — is a substantial modification, and triggers the documentation duty again. Documentation that is accurate for a superseded version does not cover the version actually in service.
requirements.title: Re-publish documentation when the system is substantially modified

controls.title: An SBOM exists in an automated format (CycloneDX or SPDX)
SBOM is generated per release, not once per company

requirements.description: An SBOM exists for each released product, service image, or significant update. A dependency screenshot or a package-lock file left in the repo is not an SBOM delivered to a buyer.
requirements.title: Produce an SBOM for each released software item

controls.title: Producer, name, and version are present on components
Component identifiers and component hash algorithm are present
Component license and dependency relationships are present
SBOM Author, Tool Name, Timestamp, and Generation Context are present

requirements.description: Each component row carries the 2026 baseline, including Component Producer, Component Name, Component Version, Component Identifiers, Component Dependency Relationship, Component Hash Algorithm, Component License, SBOM Author, SBOM Tool Name, SBOM Timestamp, and SBOM Generation Context. NTIA 2021 field names alone are stale.
requirements.title: Populate the 2026 minimum data fields

controls.title: The generating tool is named in the SBOM
SBOM generation is a release-pipeline step, not an after-the-fact memo

requirements.description: Automation remains a core 2026 practice. A spreadsheet typed at release time does not scale and will drift from the binary shipped.
requirements.title: Generate the SBOM with tooling, not by hand

controls.title: A named path exists to deliver the SBOM to the acquirer
Shared SBOMs do not embed tokens, private keys, or unpublished vulnerability details beyond the inventory

requirements.title: Be able to share the SBOM with the acquirer

controls.title: SBOM timestamp and component set match the shipped build

requirements.description: A new dependency, a patched transitive library, or a rebuilt container is a new composition. The SBOM that described the previous build does not describe the build in service.
requirements.title: Refresh the SBOM when the composition changes

controls.title: Documented testing for disparate impact across protected classes
Known and foreseeable discrimination risks documented

requirements.description: Developers and deployers must use reasonable care to protect consumers from any known or reasonably foreseeable risk of algorithmic discrimination arising from intended and contracted uses.
requirements.title: Exercise reasonable care against algorithmic discrimination

controls.title: Written risk management program mapped to a recognized framework
Program reviewed and updated on a defined cadence

requirements.description: Deployers must implement a risk management policy and program governing high-risk systems, iteratively reviewed and aligned to a recognized framework such as NIST AI RMF or ISO/IEC 42001.

controls.title: Impact assessment completed within the last 12 months
Assessments retained for at least three years

requirements.description: Deployers must complete an impact assessment annually and within 90 days of any intentional and substantial modification, covering purpose, known risks, data categories, metrics, transparency, and post-deployment monitoring.
requirements.title: Complete annual impact assessments

controls.title: Documentation package supplied to every deployer
Public statement summarizing high-risk systems and risk management

requirements.description: Developers must give deployers the information needed to complete an impact assessment: intended uses, known limitations, training data summary, evaluation and mitigation measures, and appropriate use guidance.
requirements.title: Provide documentation to deployers

controls.title: Notice delivered before the consequential decision
Notice is in plain language and accessible

requirements.description: Deployers must notify a consumer before a high-risk system makes, or is a substantial factor in making, a consequential decision, and disclose the purpose and nature of the decision.

controls.title: Principal reasons disclosed on adverse decisions
Mechanism to correct inaccurate personal data
Human review appeal path available

requirements.description: On an adverse consequential decision, the deployer must state the principal reasons, the data used and its source, and provide an opportunity to correct data and to appeal for human review where technically feasible.
requirements.title: Explain adverse decisions and offer correction and appeal

controls.title: Monitoring capable of detecting algorithmic discrimination
Documented 90-day AG notification procedure

requirements.description: On discovering that a high-risk system has caused algorithmic discrimination, the deployer must notify the Colorado Attorney General within 90 days.
requirements.title: Notify the Attorney General of discovered algorithmic discrimination

NSM-10, NIST IR guidance, and buyer contracts may incorporate it; this pack does not invent a standalone federal CBOM statute. Consult counsel and the controlling text before relying on any output.

requirements.citation: CycloneDX 1.6 § cryptographic-asset; OWASP Authoritative Guide to CBOM

controls.description: bomFormat is CycloneDX. specVersion is 1.6 or higher.
controls.title: A CycloneDX document with specVersion 1.6 or later exists

controls.description: Coverage is per system, not one company-wide PDF.
controls.title: One CBOM (or clearly scoped component set) per released system

requirements.description: A Cryptographic Bill of Materials exists for each released application, service, or firmware image that implements or consumes cryptography. A prose security whitepaper or a screenshot of OpenSSL version is not a CBOM.
requirements.title: Produce a CBOM for each released system

controls.title: Algorithms in use are listed with primitive and parameter set
Protocols in use (TLS, IPsec, SSH, etc.) are listed with version

controls.description: Private key values are not written into the CBOM. State, format, and algorithmRef are enough.
controls.title: Certificates and related material are inventoried without embedding secrets

requirements.description: Components of type cryptographic-asset declare assetType as algorithm, certificate, protocol, or related-crypto-material. Hardcoded algorithms and library-provided algorithms are both in scope.
requirements.title: Inventory cryptographic asset types

controls.title: nistQuantumSecurityLevel is present on algorithm assets

controls.description: ML-KEM / ML-DSA / SLH-DSA may carry levels 1–5. RSA and ECDH do not.
controls.title: Classical public-key algorithms are not marked as PQC

requirements.description: Each algorithm component states classicalSecurityLevel where known and nistQuantumSecurityLevel (0–5). Level 0 means the category is not met. RSA-2048 and ECDSA P-256 must not be labeled as meeting a NIST PQC category.
requirements.title: Record NIST quantum and classical security levels

controls.title: Dependency edges exist between components and cryptographic-assets

requirements.description: The CBOM records which application or library uses or provides each cryptographic asset. An algorithm listed with no parent component is an incomplete inventory.
requirements.title: Relate software components to the crypto they use or provide

requirements.citation: OWASP Authoritative Guide to CBOM; NIST crypto-agility practice

controls.title: metadata.timestamp reflects the generation event
Named owner regenerates CBOM on crypto or dependency change

requirements.description: A new library, a TLS configuration change, a certificate rotation that changes the algorithm, or a PQC hybrid rollout is a CBOM event. A CBOM dated before the last crypto change does not cover the system in service.
requirements.title: Regenerate the CBOM when cryptography changes

metadata.disclaimer: Encoded for compliance-readiness analysis, not legal advice. SBOM and CBOM obligations arise from guidance, contracts, and (for some sellers) EO 14028 procurement — not from a single combined statute. Consult counsel and the controlling text before relying on any output.

controls.title: An SBOM in CycloneDX or SPDX exists for the release
A CBOM in CycloneDX 1.6 or later exists for the same release
SBOM and CBOM describe the same shipped version

requirements.description: The released system has a Software Bill of Materials and a Cryptographic Bill of Materials. One CycloneDX 1.6 document may contain both software components and cryptographic-asset components. Two files are acceptable if they share a release identifier. An SBOM alone, or a CBOM alone, fails this requirement.
requirements.title: Produce both an SBOM and a CBOM for the released system

controls.title: 2026 minimum SBOM fields are populated

requirements.description: Component Producer, Component Name, Component Version, Component Identifiers, dependency relationships, hash algorithm, license, SBOM Author, Tool Name, Timestamp, and Generation Context are present.

requirements.citation: CycloneDX 1.6 cryptoProperties; NIST PQC security categories

controls.title: Algorithms, protocols, and certificates are inventoried
nistQuantumSecurityLevel is present on algorithm assets
RSA / ECDSA / ECDH are not marked as PQC

requirements.description: Algorithms, protocols, and certificates are listed. Algorithm assets carry nistQuantumSecurityLevel. Classical public-key algorithms are not labeled as meeting a PQC category.
requirements.title: CBOM inventories crypto assets with NIST quantum levels

controls.title: Dependency edges link cryptographic-assets to software components

requirements.description: Every cryptographic-asset points at the SBOM component that provides or uses it (for example liboqs provides ML-KEM-768; nginx uses TLS 1.3). An orphan algorithm with no parent library is an incomplete joint BOM.
requirements.title: Tie cryptographic assets to the software that implements them

requirements.citation: CycloneDX related-crypto-material practice; CISA SBOM sharing

controls.title: Private keys and tokens are absent from shared SBOM and CBOM files

requirements.description: Private keys, tokens, and raw secret values stay off the BOM. related-crypto-material records type, state, and algorithmRef only.
requirements.title: Shared BOMs do not embed secrets

requirements.citation: CISA 2026 Minimum Elements; OWASP Authoritative Guide to CBOM

controls.title: SBOM and CBOM timestamps belong to the same release
A named owner regenerates both documents on change

requirements.description: A new dependency is an SBOM event. A new cipher suite or PQC hybrid is a CBOM event. Either event refreshes the joint release pair so the two documents do not describe different builds.
requirements.title: Regenerate both BOMs when composition or cryptography changes

metadata.disclaimer: Encoded for compliance-readiness analysis, not legal advice. These controls aggregate multi-regime operational expectations; they are not a substitute for jurisdiction-specific counsel.

controls.title: Active safety circuit breaker present in production path
Documented human fallback / override endpoint
Human override is available for high-impact actions

requirements.description: Systems that can execute high-impact actions autonomously in production must expose an active safety circuit breaker and a reachable human fallback endpoint so operators can interrupt or reverse automated effects.
requirements.title: High-impact autonomous systems retain human override and fallback

controls.title: Third-party red-team evaluation completed
Red-team safety evaluation report retained and available

requirements.title: Models above 10^26 FLOPs carry third-party red-team safety evaluation

Unencrypted transfers into non-adequate jurisdictions without SCCs/BCRs fail this control.
requirements.title: Personal data transfers use adequacy, SCCs/BCRs, and encryption in transit

controls.title: Workload isolated on an air-gapped sovereign compute cluster
Workload is not executed on shared multi-tenant public clusters

requirements.description: Restricted public-sector and defense inference workloads must execute on air-gapped sovereign clusters, not shared multi-tenant public cloud tenancy.
requirements.title: Government and defense workloads run on air-gapped sovereign compute

controls.description: Every output path writes the required latent fields. Coverage across modalities matters: an image pipeline that embeds and a text pipeline that does not leaves the requirement unmet.
controls.title: Provenance metadata embedded in all generated output

controls.description: Evidence that the disclosure survives routine re-encoding, resizing, or format conversion to the extent technically feasible.
controls.title: Latent disclosure resists ordinary transformation

requirements.description: Content produced by the covered provider's system must carry a latent disclosure conveying the provider name, system name and version, the time and date of creation, and a unique identifier — detectable by the provider's own detection tool and, to the extent technically feasible, permanent or difficult to remove.
requirements.title: Embed a latent disclosure in generated content

controls.title: User-facing option to apply a visible AI disclosure

controls.description: Placement and persistence reviewed per output medium rather than asserted globally.
controls.title: Disclosure is conspicuous and permanent where technically feasible

requirements.description: The provider must make available a free, user-electable manifest disclosure that is clear, conspicuous, appropriate for the medium, and understandable to a reasonable person — identifying the content as AI-generated.
requirements.title: Offer a manifest disclosure the user can elect

controls.title: Detection tool is publicly reachable and free of charge
Tool reports system provenance data for matched content
Tool does not retain personal provenance data beyond necessity

requirements.description: The provider must make available a publicly accessible detection tool, at no cost, that lets a user assess whether content was created by the provider's system and returns any available system provenance metadata — without collecting personal provenance data beyond what is necessary.
requirements.title: Publish a free public AI detection tool

controls.title: License agreements require the latent disclosure be retained

controls.description: A written, exercisable procedure with an owner and a monitored trigger — not merely a contractual right held in reserve.
controls.title: Documented process to revoke a non-conforming license within 96 hours

requirements.description: Where a covered provider licenses its system to a third party, the license must require the latent disclosure to be maintained. On knowledge that a licensee has removed it, the provider must revoke the license within 96 hours, and the licensee must cease use on revocation.
requirements.title: Revoke licenses from third parties that strip the latent disclosure
